QRS 94 ms with very large precordial voltages (deep S in V1-V2, tall R in V5-V6) but no bundle branch block; axis about +35 degrees. QT 292 ms, QTc 398 ms. Prior tracing 7/4/2022 is essentially identical (sinus 115 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 394 ms) - no changes. Note the documented history of atrial flutter, which is not present on this tracing.

arguments.explanation: Normal sinus rhythm at 66 bpm (9/22/2025), regular. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 154 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -20 degrees (normal). QT 375 ms, QTc 394 ms. This is the only ECG on file for this patient, so no comparison is possible.

items.explanation: Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. On 7/15/2026 the cardiology clinic note documents switching rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage and starting apixaban 5 mg twice daily, but the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order was also renewed the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and never discontinued, so both apixaban 5 mg BID and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily are active as of 9/24/2026. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban confers no added benefit and a markedly increased bleeding risk in this 65-year-old man with paroxysmal/persistent AF, atrial flutter, CLL and CKD stage 3. One agent must be stopped.

56-year-old man on escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; prescribed continuously since 5/14/2024, current order 7/18/2026-12/26/2026). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 506 ms and Bazett QTc 539 ms - above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo and much longer than the QTc of ~361 ms on the previous tracing of 11/23/2022. The 5/14/2024 note records that this ECG was reviewed as 'QT acceptable', which is not supported by the measurements. Most recent electrolytes (3/18/2026) are K 3.8 mEq/L and Mg 1.9 mg/dL (both low-normal). Prescriber review and a repeat ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025 - it is absent from the 9/21/2025 medication list and first appears in the 11/10/2025 order and note. Because the start date falls between 9/1/2025 and 2/28/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies, so an ECG was due by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 558 ms, which is handled as a separate QT-safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was first prescribed at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026; there is no earlier escitalopram order for this patient. The start predates 3/1/2026, so under the 3/1/2026 revision earlier starts keep the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo and an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 3/8/2026 (24 days after the start) and showed sinus rhythm with QTc 469 ms, so the requirement was completed on time.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026 - the 12/15/2025 note lists warfarin only, and citalopram first appears in the 3/2/2026 order and note. Because the medication was started on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was obtained at the 3/7/2026 clinic visit (5 days after the start) and showed sinus rhythm with QTc 385 ms, so the requirement was completed on time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026 (first escitalopram order for this patient). Started after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo's 14-day window applies and an ECG was due by 4/24/2026. No ECG was recorded within that window - the only tracing on file (107859369) was obtained on 4/29/2026, five days after the deadline - so the required post-initiation monitoring was not completed in time and is overdue. Subsequent refills on 6/20/2026 and 8/11/2026 continued the drug without a timely baseline ECG.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026 - the 2/18/2026 clinic note lists only aspirin and atorvastatin, and the outpatient escitalopram order and medication list date from 8/1/2026 (an inpatient course in late 12/2025 had ended). The start is after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the only tracing on file is from 12/25/2025), so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was restarted/started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026 (prior use was a brief inpatient course in 2024). Started after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing falls inside the required window and could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026; previous haloperidol exposure was parenteral during an inpatient stay in Feb-Mar 2025. Started after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 3/9/2025, but the deadline falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due. It should be tracked so the ECG is obtained by 9/29/2026 (baseline 3/9/2025 tracing: sinus rhythm, QTc 417 ms).

At the cardiology clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr Kessler documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily with a plan to recheck the INR. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was completed within the required time.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily for a home INR of 3.4, a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist under the anticoagulation standing order. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since 6/17/2026 (INR 2.7); nothing was drawn after the dose change, so the required INR is overdue as of 9/24/2026 - particularly important in a 95-year-old on concomitant amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.

Apixaban 5 mg is currently ordered (renewed 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027) even though the outside-records summary of 8/12/2026 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL requiring 2 units of transfusion, and states that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. The chart contains no documented cardiology decision to resume it, yet the 8/20/2026 clinic note again lists apixaban (plus aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, i.e. triple therapy) as a current medication. Anticoagulation after a recent major GI bleed, with concomitant dual antiplatelet therapy, should not continue without explicit prescriber review of indication (atrial flutter), timing of resumption and antithrombotic de-escalation.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm - new atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The clinical course supports the ECGs (she was admitted that evening and given IV metoprolol, digoxin, heparin and enoxaparin, and atrial fibrillation was coded for the admission). The note needs correction and the documented rhythm reconciled with the tracings.

71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (problem list and every cardiology clinic note, most recently 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no diabetes, heart failure or prior stroke. A score of 3 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant has ever been prescribed: the only current medication is levothyroxine 50 mcg daily (previous regimens were tamsulosin/levothyroxine only). A prior 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is on the problem list and should be weighed, but it does not remove the indication - stroke-prevention therapy needs to be discussed and started or a documented reason for withholding it recorded.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0) and a prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis, dysarthria and ataxia. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1) - a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, and secondary stroke prevention at that. Current medications are metoprolol tartrate 25 mg, levothyroxine and famotidine only; no anticoagulant is ordered and none appears anywhere in the medication history. Thrombocytopenia is also on the problem list, so platelet count/bleeding risk should be reviewed as part of the anticoagulation decision.

80-year-old woman carried in every cardiology clinic note (most recently 6/22/2026) as having persistent atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (congestive heart failure - hypertensive heart disease with heart failure / acute-on-chronic combined systolic and diastolic HF 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual right hemiparesis and dysarthria 2, vascular disease - atherosclerotic coronary disease and old myocardial infarction 1, female 1). Despite this very high thromboembolic risk her only current medications are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin; aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis in AF. Oral anticoagulation is a Class 1 recommendation and needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

48-year-old man carried as having paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in all cardiology clinic notes (most recently 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (history of congestive heart failure - acute systolic heart failure/CHF and other primary cardiomyopathy on the problem list 1; essential hypertension 1); he is under 65, not diabetic and has no prior stroke. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, yet his only current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline, and 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' on the problem list is historical only. Anticoagulation (or a documented reason to withhold it, e.g. prior thrombocytopenia/bleeding) should be addressed; note his most recent ECG (7/15/2025) was in sinus rhythm, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

79-year-old man on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, currently ordered 7/12/2026-1/9/2027, started at the 11/10/2025 cardiology clinic visit). His most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 549 ms and Bazett QTc 558 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, and up from QTc ~415 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing before amiodarone was started. Electrolytes are not contributory (K 4.3 mEq/L and Mg 2.1 mg/dL, both 6/9/2026). He is also on warfarin, clopidogrel and aspirin. Prescriber review of amiodarone (dose/continuation) and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman on long-term amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 6/17/2026-1/11/2027). Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a markedly prolonged and broad T wave, QT 585 ms and Bazett QTc 573 ms - far above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent electrolytes (6/17/2026) are K 4.2 mEq/L and Mg 1.9 mg/dL, so hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia do not explain it. She also takes metoprolol succinate (bradycardia) and warfarin. Prescriber review of amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required - the only tracing on file is more than four years old.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; continuously prescribed since 10/2/2023, current order 7/15/2026-1/7/2027). Her most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 513 ms and Bazett QTc 553 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) is normal; the most recent magnesium is 2.0 mg/dL from 3/8/2025. Citalopram 40 mg exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised where QT prolongation is a concern; prescriber review of dose/continuation and a repeat ECG with electrolytes are required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF with negative P in aVR precede every QRS at a constant PR of about 165 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -5 degrees (normal). QT 393 ms, Bazett QTc 369 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 12/13/2018 (sinus rhythm 66 bpm, QRS 100 ms, QTc 391 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 22 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm (10/8/2023), regular, PR about 132 ms with upright P in II/III/aVF and a negative P component in V1/aVR. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +47 degrees. The T wave is broad and late: QT 506 ms with Bazett QTc 539 ms - significant QT prolongation in a patient subsequently maintained on escitalopram. The prior tracing of 11/23/2022 showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with QT 324 ms and QTc 361 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (11/10/2023). Upright P waves in I/II/aVF, negative in aVR, PR about 160 ms. QRS 98 ms - upper normal, no bundle branch block pattern. Frontal axis about +34 degrees. The T wave is low, broad and very late (peak about 370 ms after the QRS) giving QT 513 ms and Bazett QTc 553 ms, i.e. marked QT prolongation in a patient on citalopram 40 mg daily. The prior tracing of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc about 450 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (4/19/2024), RR regular (coefficient of variation 0.01). Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede every QRS with PR about 130 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). QT 305 ms with Bazett QTc 433 ms. This is the only ECG on file for this patient, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm (5/21/2024), regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 115 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +36 degrees. QT 349 ms, Bazett QTc 472 ms - borderline prolonged, partly rate-related given the tachycardia. No prior ECG is available for this patient.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm (5/23/2024), regular. Discrete upright P waves in II/III/aVF before each QRS, PR about 112 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +6 degrees. QT 316 ms, QTc 402 ms - normal. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (7/17/2024) with first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS but the PR interval is prolonged at about 208 ms. QRS is wide at 128 ms with a broad monophasic R in I, aVL and V6, absent septal q, and deep QS complexes in V1-V2 - a typical LBBB pattern. Frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal). QT 450 ms, QTc 452 ms. The prior tracing of 6/3/2024 showed the same pattern (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 210 ms, LBBB with QRS 128 ms, QTc 459 ms), so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Atrial fibrillation (9/17/2024). The ventricular response is irregularly irregular with RR intervals ranging from 0.39 to 1.09 s (coefficient of variation 0.29, RMSSD 264 ms) and a mean rate of about 99 bpm; no P waves are identifiable and the baseline is fibrillatory, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -53 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 337 ms, QTc 432 ms. This is the only ECG on file for this patient, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm (10/24/2024) in a patient with a history of atrial fibrillation - the fibrillation is not present on this tracing. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF, negative in aVR and V1, precede every QRS with PR about 173 ms. QRS 90 ms with tall R waves in V5-V6 but no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +37 degrees. QT about 440 ms, Bazett QTc about 405 ms. Prior tracing 5/22/2023: sinus rhythm 57 bpm with a single ectopic beat, QRS 84 ms, QTc 392 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Atrial fibrillation with a moderate/slow ventricular response (11/15/2024). Ten QRS complexes in 10 seconds (mean rate about 61 bpm) with markedly irregular RR intervals from 0.69 to 1.16 s (RMSSD 288 ms) and no identifiable P waves before any complex, so no PR interval. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +27 degrees. QT 461 ms, QTc 434 ms. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear upright P waves and PR about 175 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (12/5/2024, 14:38), RR extremely regular. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede every QRS with PR about 130 ms. QRS duration is now normal at 92 ms with an RS pattern in lead I and low overall voltages; the net frontal vector is rightward (axis roughly +130 degrees, right axis deviation). QT 297 ms, QTc 422 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (01:33) showed sinus rhythm at 100 bpm with a wide QRS of 152 ms, an rSR' with a broad terminal R in V1-V2 and terminal S waves in I/V6 - right bundle branch block - which is no longer present, so the bundle branch block has resolved. QTc change (477 to 422 ms) is less than 60 ms.

Normal sinus rhythm at 77 bpm (6/19/2020). Prominent upright P waves in II/III/aVF, negative in aVR, PR about 150 ms and constant. Narrow QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal). QT 409 ms, QTc (Bazett) 462 ms - mildly prolonged, with a long low-amplitude terminal T/U component. Prior tracing 2/2/2020 also showed sinus rhythm with frequent short-coupled ectopic beats (couplets); rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QT on that low-amplitude, ectopy-laden tracing is not reliably comparable, so no significant interval change is reported.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm (2/15/2025), regular. Upright P waves in I/II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 180 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +55 degrees. QT 384 ms, QTc 426 ms - normal. No prior ECG is available for this patient.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm (3/9/2025). Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS with a short-normal PR of about 110 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +60 degrees. QT 423 ms, QTc 417 ms. Prior tracing 3/8/2025: sinus rhythm 62 bpm, PR 110 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 442 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. This is the baseline tracing preceding the haloperidol start of 9/15/2026.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (3/14/2025) with a single early ectopic beat and compensatory pause (RR 0.98 s throughout apart from a 0.54 s/1.37 s couplet), so the underlying rhythm is regular sinus rather than atrial fibrillation. A low-amplitude P wave, best seen in lead I, precedes each QRS with PR about 190 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT 391 ms, QTc 395 ms. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible - relevant because the patient carries a diagnosis of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm (3/19/2025), regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 136 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +44 degrees. QT 335 ms, QTc 436 ms. Prior tracing 3/18/2025: sinus rhythm 102 bpm, PR 128 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 432 ms - unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm (5/12/2025), regular. Upright P waves in I/II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 158 ms. QRS 100 ms - upper limit of normal, without an RBBB or LBBB pattern. Frontal axis about +30 degrees. QT 381 ms, QTc 446 ms. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm (6/23/2025), regular. An upright P wave in II/III/aVF precedes each QRS with PR about 115 ms. QRS 82 ms with prominent R in V1 and tall R in V6 but no bundle branch block; frontal axis within the normal range. QT 401 ms, QTc 382 ms. Prior tracing 11/30/2024: sinus rhythm 51 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 365 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm (7/15/2025), RR regular. A discrete upright P wave in II/aVF (negative in V1) precedes each QRS with PR about 128 ms. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +30 degrees. QT 350 ms, Bazett QTc 460 ms (mildly prolonged, in part rate-related). Prior tracing 6/20/2025: sinus tachycardia 147 bpm with fused T and P waves, QRS 92 ms, QTc 432 ms - rhythm and conduction unchanged, QTc difference less than 60 ms. Notably, neither tracing shows the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in the problem list.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (8/2/2025) that is not sinus: each QRS is preceded by a P wave that is inverted in II, III and aVF and upright in I and aVL (P axis roughly -60 degrees), i.e. an ectopic low-atrial (or coronary-sinus) rhythm, with a PR of about 155 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT 414 ms, QTc 444 ms. The prior tracing of 4/27/2025 shows the same ectopic atrial P-wave morphology but was recorded with right/left arm lead reversal (lead I inverted with upright aVR); after correcting for the reversal the rhythm, conduction and QTc (408 ms) are unchanged.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm (8/23/2025), RR very regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 146 ms. Narrow QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +52 degrees. QT 347 ms, QTc 410 ms - normal. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (9/13/2025). Twenty-five QRS complexes in 10 seconds with grossly irregular RR intervals from 0.29 to 0.58 s (coefficient of variation 0.19, RMSSD 104 ms), mean ventricular rate about 153 bpm, an undulating baseline and no identifiable P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -20 degrees. QT 270 ms, QTc 430 ms. The prior tracing of 9/12/2025 showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with upright P waves and PR about 150 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation (IV then oral amiodarone was given over the following days).

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm (1/18/2021), RR interval very regular (0.50 s). A discrete upright P wave in II/aVF with negative deflection in aVR precedes each QRS; PR about 190 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 92 ms with tall R in V5 and deep S in V2 but no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +50 degrees. QT 280 ms, QTc 396 ms. Prior tracing 9/16/2016 showed sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 172 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 406 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm (8/23/2021), regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF preceding each QRS, PR about 145 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +58 degrees. QT 328 ms, QTc 427 ms. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (100 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 420 ms) and is essentially identical - no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm (4/27/2022) in a patient on chronic amiodarone. Upright P in II/aVF before every QRS, PR about 195 ms (upper normal). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +36 degrees. The T wave is broad and markedly delayed with QT 585 ms and Bazett QTc 573 ms - marked QT prolongation, typical of amiodarone effect. The prior tracing of 4/6/2022 showed atrial fibrillation with an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 131 bpm and no P waves (QTc about 463 ms); the current tracing has organised into sinus rhythm, so AF has resolved, and the QTc is more than 60 ms longer than on the prior study.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm (5/1/2022), RR very regular. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS with a short-normal PR of about 115 ms. Narrow QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +50 degrees. QT 328 ms, QTc 438 ms. Prior tracing 7/27/2019: sinus rhythm 75 bpm, PR 114 ms, QRS 70 ms, QTc 430 ms - rhythm, conduction and QTc unchanged.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 AV conduction (7/13/2022). The ventricular response is regular at 141 bpm (RR 0.43 s, coefficient of variation 0.02) and there are regular saw-tooth atrial deflections about every 205 ms (atrial rate roughly 290/min), one just after the QRS and one in late diastole, best seen in II/III/aVF and V1; there is no isoelectric baseline and no true sinus P wave, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +2 degrees. QT 274 ms, QTc 420 ms. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, mean rate about 110 bpm, no organised atrial activity), so the fibrillation has organised into new atrial flutter.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm (7/16/2022), regular. A low-amplitude but definite upright P wave in II/III/aVF (biphasic in V1, negative in aVR) precedes each QRS with PR about 180 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -19 degrees (normal). QT 339 ms, QTc 417 ms. Prior tracing 5/16/2021: sinus rhythm 87 bpm, QRS 82 ms, QTc 397 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm (6/26/2023), RR regular. An upright P wave in II/III/aVF with a negative component in aVR precedes each QRS at a PR of about 160 ms, with a clearly isoelectric PR segment (no flutter waves). QRS 94 ms with very large precordial voltages (deep S in V1-V2, tall R in V5-V6) but no bundle branch block; axis about +35 degrees. QT 292 ms, QTc 398 ms. Prior tracing 7/4/2022 is essentially identical (sinus 115 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 394 ms) - no changes. Note the documented history of atrial flutter, which is not present on this tracing.

Because the start date falls between 9/1/2025 and 2/28/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies, so an ECG was due by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 558 ms, which is handled as a separate QT-safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was first prescribed at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026; there is no earlier escitalopram order for this patient. The start predates 3/1/2026, so under the 3/1/2026 revision earlier starts keep the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo and an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 3/8/2026 (24 days after the start) and showed sinus rhythm with QTc 469 ms, so the requirement was completed on time.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026 - the 12/15/2025 note lists warfarin only, and citalopram first appears in the 3/2/2026 order and note. Because the medication was started on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was obtained at the 3/7/2026 clinic visit (5 days after the start) and showed sinus rhythm with QTc 385 ms, so the requirement was completed on time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026 (first escitalopram order for this patient). Started after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo's 14-day window applies and an ECG was due by 4/24/2026. No ECG was recorded within that window - the only tracing on file (107859369) was obtained on 4/29/2026, five days after the deadline - so the required post-initiation monitoring was not completed in time and is overdue. Subsequent refills on 6/20/2026 and 8/11/2026 continued the drug without a timely baseline ECG.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026 - the 2/18/2026 clinic note lists only aspirin and atorvastatin, and the outpatient escitalopram order and medication list date from 8/1/2026 (an inpatient course in late 12/2025 had ended). The start is after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the only tracing on file is from 12/25/2025), so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was restarted/started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026 (prior use was a brief inpatient course in 2024). Started after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing falls inside the required window and could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026; previous haloperidol exposure was parenteral during an inpatient stay in Feb-Mar 2025. Started after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 3/9/2025, but the deadline falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due. It should be tracked so the ECG is obtained by 9/29/2026 (baseline 3/9/2025 tracing: sinus rhythm, QTc 417 ms).

At the cardiology clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr Kessler documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily with a plan to recheck the INR. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was completed within the required time.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily for a home INR of 3.4, a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist under the anticoagulation standing order. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since 6/17/2026 (INR 2.7); nothing was drawn after the dose change, so the required INR is overdue as of 9/24/2026 - particularly important in a 95-year-old on concomitant amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.

Apixaban 5 mg is currently ordered (renewed 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027) even though the outside-records summary of 8/12/2026 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL requiring 2 units of transfusion, and states that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. The chart contains no documented cardiology decision to resume it, yet the 8/20/2026 clinic note again lists apixaban (plus aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, i.e. triple therapy) as a current medication. Anticoagulation after a recent major GI bleed, with concomitant dual antiplatelet therapy, should not continue without explicit prescriber review of indication (atrial flutter), timing of resumption and antithrombotic de-escalation.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm - new atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The clinical course supports the ECGs (she was admitted that evening and given IV metoprolol, digoxin, heparin and enoxaparin, and atrial fibrillation was coded for the admission). The note needs correction and the documented rhythm reconciled with the tracings.

71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (problem list and every cardiology clinic note, most recently 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no diabetes, heart failure or prior stroke. A score of 3 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant has ever been prescribed: the only current medication is levothyroxine 50 mcg daily (previous regimens were tamsulosin/levothyroxine only). A prior 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is on the problem list and should be weighed, but it does not remove the indication - stroke-prevention therapy needs to be discussed and started or a documented reason for withholding it recorded.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0) and a prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis, dysarthria and ataxia. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1) - a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, and secondary stroke prevention at that. Current medications are metoprolol tartrate 25 mg, levothyroxine and famotidine only; no anticoagulant is ordered and none appears anywhere in the medication history. Thrombocytopenia is also on the problem list, so platelet count/bleeding risk should be reviewed as part of the anticoagulation decision.

80-year-old woman carried in every cardiology clinic note (most recently 6/22/2026) as having persistent atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (congestive heart failure - hypertensive heart disease with heart failure / acute-on-chronic combined systolic and diastolic HF 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual right hemiparesis and dysarthria 2, vascular disease - atherosclerotic coronary disease and old myocardial infarction 1, female 1). Despite this very high thromboembolic risk her only current medications are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin; aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis in AF. Oral anticoagulation is a Class 1 recommendation and needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

48-year-old man carried as having paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in all cardiology clinic notes (most recently 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (history of congestive heart failure - acute systolic heart failure/CHF and other primary cardiomyopathy on the problem list 1; essential hypertension 1); he is under 65, not diabetic and has no prior stroke. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, yet his only current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline, and 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' on the problem list is historical only. Anticoagulation (or a documented reason to withhold it, e.g. prior thrombocytopenia/bleeding) should be addressed; note his most recent ECG (7/15/2025) was in sinus rhythm, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

79-year-old man on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, currently ordered 7/12/2026-1/9/2027, started at the 11/10/2025 cardiology clinic visit). His most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 549 ms and Bazett QTc 558 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, and up from QTc ~415 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing before amiodarone was started. Electrolytes are not contributory (K 4.3 mEq/L and Mg 2.1 mg/dL, both 6/9/2026). He is also on warfarin, clopidogrel and aspirin. Prescriber review of amiodarone (dose/continuation) and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman on long-term amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 6/17/2026-1/11/2027). Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a markedly prolonged and broad T wave, QT 585 ms and Bazett QTc 573 ms - far above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent electrolytes (6/17/2026) are K 4.2 mEq/L and Mg 1.9 mg/dL, so hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia do not explain it. She also takes metoprolol succinate (bradycardia) and warfarin. Prescriber review of amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required - the only tracing on file is more than four years old.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; continuously prescribed since 10/2/2023, current order 7/15/2026-1/7/2027). Her most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 513 ms and Bazett QTc 553 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) is normal; the most recent magnesium is 2.0 mg/dL from 3/8/2025. Citalopram 40 mg exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised where QT prolongation is a concern; prescriber review of dose/continuation and a repeat ECG with electrolytes are required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF with negative P in aVR precede every QRS at a constant PR of about 165 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -5 degrees (normal). QT 393 ms, Bazett QTc 369 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 12/13/2018 (sinus rhythm 66 bpm, QRS 100 ms, QTc 391 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 22 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm (10/8/2023), regular, PR about 132 ms with upright P in II/III/aVF and a negative P component in V1/aVR. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +47 degrees. The T wave is broad and late: QT 506 ms with Bazett QTc 539 ms - significant QT prolongation in a patient subsequently maintained on escitalopram. The prior tracing of 11/23/2022 showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with QT 324 ms and QTc 361 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (11/10/2023). Upright P waves in I/II/aVF, negative in aVR, PR about 160 ms. QRS 98 ms - upper normal, no bundle branch block pattern. Frontal axis about +34 degrees. The T wave is low, broad and very late (peak about 370 ms after the QRS) giving QT 513 ms and Bazett QTc 553 ms, i.e. marked QT prolongation in a patient on citalopram 40 mg daily. The prior tracing of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc about 450 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (4/19/2024), RR regular (coefficient of variation 0.01). Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede every QRS with PR about 130 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). QT 305 ms with Bazett QTc 433 ms. This is the only ECG on file for this patient, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm (5/21/2024), regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 115 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +36 degrees. QT 349 ms, Bazett QTc 472 ms - borderline prolonged, partly rate-related given the tachycardia. No prior ECG is available for this patient.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm (5/23/2024), regular. Discrete upright P waves in II/III/aVF before each QRS, PR about 112 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +6 degrees. QT 316 ms, QTc 402 ms - normal. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (7/17/2024) with first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS but the PR interval is prolonged at about 208 ms. QRS is wide at 128 ms with a broad monophasic R in I, aVL and V6, absent septal q, and deep QS complexes in V1-V2 - a typical LBBB pattern. Frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal). QT 450 ms, QTc 452 ms. The prior tracing of 6/3/2024 showed the same pattern (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 210 ms, LBBB with QRS 128 ms, QTc 459 ms), so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Atrial fibrillation (9/17/2024). The ventricular response is irregularly irregular with RR intervals ranging from 0.39 to 1.09 s (coefficient of variation 0.29, RMSSD 264 ms) and a mean rate of about 99 bpm; no P waves are identifiable and the baseline is fibrillatory, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -53 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 337 ms, QTc 432 ms. This is the only ECG on file for this patient, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm (10/24/2024) in a patient with a history of atrial fibrillation - the fibrillation is not present on this tracing. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF, negative in aVR and V1, precede every QRS with PR about 173 ms. QRS 90 ms with tall R waves in V5-V6 but no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +37 degrees. QT about 440 ms, Bazett QTc about 405 ms. Prior tracing 5/22/2023: sinus rhythm 57 bpm with a single ectopic beat, QRS 84 ms, QTc 392 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Atrial fibrillation with a moderate/slow ventricular response (11/15/2024). Ten QRS complexes in 10 seconds (mean rate about 61 bpm) with markedly irregular RR intervals from 0.69 to 1.16 s (RMSSD 288 ms) and no identifiable P waves before any complex, so no PR interval. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +27 degrees. QT 461 ms, QTc 434 ms. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear upright P waves and PR about 175 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (12/5/2024, 14:38), RR extremely regular. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede every QRS with PR about 130 ms. QRS duration is now normal at 92 ms with an RS pattern in lead I and low overall voltages; the net frontal vector is rightward (axis roughly +130 degrees, right axis deviation). QT 297 ms, QTc 422 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (01:33) showed sinus rhythm at 100 bpm with a wide QRS of 152 ms, an rSR' with a broad terminal R in V1-V2 and terminal S waves in I/V6 - right bundle branch block - which is no longer present, so the bundle branch block has resolved. QTc change (477 to 422 ms) is less than 60 ms.

Normal sinus rhythm at 77 bpm (6/19/2020). Prominent upright P waves in II/III/aVF, negative in aVR, PR about 150 ms and constant. Narrow QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal). QT 409 ms, QTc (Bazett) 462 ms - mildly prolonged, with a long low-amplitude terminal T/U component. Prior tracing 2/2/2020 also showed sinus rhythm with frequent short-coupled ectopic beats (couplets); rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QT on that low-amplitude, ectopy-laden tracing is not reliably comparable, so no significant interval change is reported.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm (2/15/2025), regular. Upright P waves in I/II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 180 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +55 degrees. QT 384 ms, QTc 426 ms - normal. No prior ECG is available for this patient.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm (3/9/2025). Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS with a short-normal PR of about 110 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +60 degrees. QT 423 ms, QTc 417 ms. Prior tracing 3/8/2025: sinus rhythm 62 bpm, PR 110 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 442 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. This is the baseline tracing preceding the haloperidol start of 9/15/2026.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (3/14/2025) with a single early ectopic beat and compensatory pause (RR 0.98 s throughout apart from a 0.54 s/1.37 s couplet), so the underlying rhythm is regular sinus rather than atrial fibrillation. A low-amplitude P wave, best seen in lead I, precedes each QRS with PR about 190 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT 391 ms, QTc 395 ms. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible - relevant because the patient carries a diagnosis of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm (3/19/2025), regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 136 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +44 degrees. QT 335 ms, QTc 436 ms. Prior tracing 3/18/2025: sinus rhythm 102 bpm, PR 128 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 432 ms - unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm (5/12/2025), regular. Upright P waves in I/II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 158 ms. QRS 100 ms - upper limit of normal, without an RBBB or LBBB pattern. Frontal axis about +30 degrees. QT 381 ms, QTc 446 ms. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm (6/23/2025), regular. An upright P wave in II/III/aVF precedes each QRS with PR about 115 ms. QRS 82 ms with prominent R in V1 and tall R in V6 but no bundle branch block; frontal axis within the normal range. QT 401 ms, QTc 382 ms. Prior tracing 11/30/2024: sinus rhythm 51 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 365 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm (7/15/2025), RR regular. A discrete upright P wave in II/aVF (negative in V1) precedes each QRS with PR about 128 ms. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +30 degrees. QT 350 ms, Bazett QTc 460 ms (mildly prolonged, in part rate-related). Prior tracing 6/20/2025: sinus tachycardia 147 bpm with fused T and P waves, QRS 92 ms, QTc 432 ms - rhythm and conduction unchanged, QTc difference less than 60 ms. Notably, neither tracing shows the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in the problem list.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (8/2/2025) that is not sinus: each QRS is preceded by a P wave that is inverted in II, III and aVF and upright in I and aVL (P axis roughly -60 degrees), i.e. an ectopic low-atrial (or coronary-sinus) rhythm, with a PR of about 155 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT 414 ms, QTc 444 ms. The prior tracing of 4/27/2025 shows the same ectopic atrial P-wave morphology but was recorded with right/left arm lead reversal (lead I inverted with upright aVR); after correcting for the reversal the rhythm, conduction and QTc (408 ms) are unchanged.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm (8/23/2025), RR very regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 146 ms. Narrow QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +52 degrees. QT 347 ms, QTc 410 ms - normal. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (9/13/2025). Twenty-five QRS complexes in 10 seconds with grossly irregular RR intervals from 0.29 to 0.58 s (coefficient of variation 0.19, RMSSD 104 ms), mean ventricular rate about 153 bpm, an undulating baseline and no identifiable P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -20 degrees. QT 270 ms, QTc 430 ms. The prior tracing of 9/12/2025 showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with upright P waves and PR about 150 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation (IV then oral amiodarone was given over the following days).

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm (1/18/2021), RR interval very regular (0.50 s). A discrete upright P wave in II/aVF with negative deflection in aVR precedes each QRS; PR about 190 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 92 ms with tall R in V5 and deep S in V2 but no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +50 degrees. QT 280 ms, QTc 396 ms. Prior tracing 9/16/2016 showed sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 172 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 406 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Normal sinus rhythm at 66 bpm (9/22/2025), regular. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 154 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -20 degrees (normal). QT 375 ms, QTc 394 ms. This is the only ECG on file for this patient, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm (8/23/2021), regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF preceding each QRS, PR about 145 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +58 degrees. QT 328 ms, QTc 427 ms. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (100 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 420 ms) and is essentially identical - no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm (4/27/2022) in a patient on chronic amiodarone. Upright P in II/aVF before every QRS, PR about 195 ms (upper normal). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +36 degrees. The T wave is broad and markedly delayed with QT 585 ms and Bazett QTc 573 ms - marked QT prolongation, typical of amiodarone effect. The prior tracing of 4/6/2022 showed atrial fibrillation with an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 131 bpm and no P waves (QTc about 463 ms); the current tracing has organised into sinus rhythm, so AF has resolved, and the QTc is more than 60 ms longer than on the prior study.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm (5/1/2022), RR very regular. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS with a short-normal PR of about 115 ms. Narrow QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +50 degrees. QT 328 ms, QTc 438 ms. Prior tracing 7/27/2019: sinus rhythm 75 bpm, PR 114 ms, QRS 70 ms, QTc 430 ms - rhythm, conduction and QTc unchanged.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 AV conduction (7/13/2022). The ventricular response is regular at 141 bpm (RR 0.43 s, coefficient of variation 0.02) and there are regular saw-tooth atrial deflections about every 205 ms (atrial rate roughly 290/min), one just after the QRS and one in late diastole, best seen in II/III/aVF and V1; there is no isoelectric baseline and no true sinus P wave, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +2 degrees. QT 274 ms, QTc 420 ms. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, mean rate about 110 bpm, no organised atrial activity), so the fibrillation has organised into new atrial flutter.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm (7/16/2022), regular. A low-amplitude but definite upright P wave in II/III/aVF (biphasic in V1, negative in aVR) precedes each QRS with PR about 180 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -19 degrees (normal). QT 339 ms, QTc 417 ms. Prior tracing 5/16/2021: sinus rhythm 87 bpm, QRS 82 ms, QTc 397 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm (6/26/2023), RR regular. An upright P wave in II/III/aVF with a negative component in aVR precedes each QRS at a PR of about 160 ms, with a clearly isoelectric PR segment (no flutter waves). QRS 94 ms with very large precordial voltages (deep S in V1-V2, tall R in V5-V6) but no bundle branch block; axis about +35 degrees. QT 292 ms, QTc 398 ms. Prior tracing 7/4/2022 is essentially identical (sinus 115 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 394 ms) - no changes. Note the documented history of atrial flutter, which is not present on this tracing.

arguments.explanation: Normal sinus rhythm at 73 bpm (11/23/2025), consistent with the same-day clinic note. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF with negative P in aVR precede each QRS at a PR of about 165 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +12 degrees. QT 360 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms. On the prior tracing of 11/21/2025 the rhythm and conduction were the same (sinus 67 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 88 ms) but repolarisation was markedly delayed with QT 509 ms and QTc 539 ms; the QTc has therefore shortened by more than 60 ms and is now normal.

items.explanation: Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. On 7/15/2026 the cardiology clinic note documents switching rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage and starting apixaban 5 mg twice daily, but the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order was also renewed the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and never discontinued, so both apixaban 5 mg BID and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily are active as of 9/24/2026. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban confers no added benefit and a markedly increased bleeding risk in this 65-year-old man with paroxysmal/persistent AF, atrial flutter, CLL and CKD stage 3. One agent must be stopped.

56-year-old man on escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; prescribed continuously since 5/14/2024, current order 7/18/2026-12/26/2026). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 506 ms and Bazett QTc 539 ms - above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo and much longer than the QTc of ~361 ms on the previous tracing of 11/23/2022. The 5/14/2024 note records that this ECG was reviewed as 'QT acceptable', which is not supported by the measurements. Most recent electrolytes (3/18/2026) are K 3.8 mEq/L and Mg 1.9 mg/dL (both low-normal). Prescriber review and a repeat ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025 - it is absent from the 9/21/2025 medication list and first appears in the 11/10/2025 order and note. Because the start date falls between 9/1/2025 and 2/28/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies, so an ECG was due by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 558 ms, which is handled as a separate QT-safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was first prescribed at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026; there is no earlier escitalopram order for this patient. The start predates 3/1/2026, so under the 3/1/2026 revision earlier starts keep the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo and an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 3/8/2026 (24 days after the start) and showed sinus rhythm with QTc 469 ms, so the requirement was completed on time.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026 - the 12/15/2025 note lists warfarin only, and citalopram first appears in the 3/2/2026 order and note. Because the medication was started on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was obtained at the 3/7/2026 clinic visit (5 days after the start) and showed sinus rhythm with QTc 385 ms, so the requirement was completed on time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026 (first escitalopram order for this patient). Started after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo's 14-day window applies and an ECG was due by 4/24/2026. No ECG was recorded within that window - the only tracing on file (107859369) was obtained on 4/29/2026, five days after the deadline - so the required post-initiation monitoring was not completed in time and is overdue. Subsequent refills on 6/20/2026 and 8/11/2026 continued the drug without a timely baseline ECG.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026 - the 2/18/2026 clinic note lists only aspirin and atorvastatin, and the outpatient escitalopram order and medication list date from 8/1/2026 (an inpatient course in late 12/2025 had ended). The start is after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the only tracing on file is from 12/25/2025), so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was restarted/started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026 (prior use was a brief inpatient course in 2024). Started after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing falls inside the required window and could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026; previous haloperidol exposure was parenteral during an inpatient stay in Feb-Mar 2025. Started after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 3/9/2025, but the deadline falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due. It should be tracked so the ECG is obtained by 9/29/2026 (baseline 3/9/2025 tracing: sinus rhythm, QTc 417 ms).

At the cardiology clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr Kessler documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily with a plan to recheck the INR. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was completed within the required time.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily for a home INR of 3.4, a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist under the anticoagulation standing order. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since 6/17/2026 (INR 2.7); nothing was drawn after the dose change, so the required INR is overdue as of 9/24/2026 - particularly important in a 95-year-old on concomitant amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.

Apixaban 5 mg is currently ordered (renewed 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027) even though the outside-records summary of 8/12/2026 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL requiring 2 units of transfusion, and states that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. The chart contains no documented cardiology decision to resume it, yet the 8/20/2026 clinic note again lists apixaban (plus aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, i.e. triple therapy) as a current medication. Anticoagulation after a recent major GI bleed, with concomitant dual antiplatelet therapy, should not continue without explicit prescriber review of indication (atrial flutter), timing of resumption and antithrombotic de-escalation.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm - new atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The clinical course supports the ECGs (she was admitted that evening and given IV metoprolol, digoxin, heparin and enoxaparin, and atrial fibrillation was coded for the admission). The note needs correction and the documented rhythm reconciled with the tracings.

71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (problem list and every cardiology clinic note, most recently 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no diabetes, heart failure or prior stroke. A score of 3 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant has ever been prescribed: the only current medication is levothyroxine 50 mcg daily (previous regimens were tamsulosin/levothyroxine only). A prior 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is on the problem list and should be weighed, but it does not remove the indication - stroke-prevention therapy needs to be discussed and started or a documented reason for withholding it recorded.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0) and a prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis, dysarthria and ataxia. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1) - a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, and secondary stroke prevention at that. Current medications are metoprolol tartrate 25 mg, levothyroxine and famotidine only; no anticoagulant is ordered and none appears anywhere in the medication history. Thrombocytopenia is also on the problem list, so platelet count/bleeding risk should be reviewed as part of the anticoagulation decision.

80-year-old woman carried in every cardiology clinic note (most recently 6/22/2026) as having persistent atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (congestive heart failure - hypertensive heart disease with heart failure / acute-on-chronic combined systolic and diastolic HF 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual right hemiparesis and dysarthria 2, vascular disease - atherosclerotic coronary disease and old myocardial infarction 1, female 1). Despite this very high thromboembolic risk her only current medications are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin; aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis in AF. Oral anticoagulation is a Class 1 recommendation and needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

48-year-old man carried as having paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in all cardiology clinic notes (most recently 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (history of congestive heart failure - acute systolic heart failure/CHF and other primary cardiomyopathy on the problem list 1; essential hypertension 1); he is under 65, not diabetic and has no prior stroke. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, yet his only current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline, and 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' on the problem list is historical only. Anticoagulation (or a documented reason to withhold it, e.g. prior thrombocytopenia/bleeding) should be addressed; note his most recent ECG (7/15/2025) was in sinus rhythm, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

79-year-old man on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, currently ordered 7/12/2026-1/9/2027, started at the 11/10/2025 cardiology clinic visit). His most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 549 ms and Bazett QTc 558 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, and up from QTc ~415 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing before amiodarone was started. Electrolytes are not contributory (K 4.3 mEq/L and Mg 2.1 mg/dL, both 6/9/2026). He is also on warfarin, clopidogrel and aspirin. Prescriber review of amiodarone (dose/continuation) and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman on long-term amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 6/17/2026-1/11/2027). Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a markedly prolonged and broad T wave, QT 585 ms and Bazett QTc 573 ms - far above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent electrolytes (6/17/2026) are K 4.2 mEq/L and Mg 1.9 mg/dL, so hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia do not explain it. She also takes metoprolol succinate (bradycardia) and warfarin. Prescriber review of amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required - the only tracing on file is more than four years old.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; continuously prescribed since 10/2/2023, current order 7/15/2026-1/7/2027). Her most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 513 ms and Bazett QTc 553 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) is normal; the most recent magnesium is 2.0 mg/dL from 3/8/2025. Citalopram 40 mg exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised where QT prolongation is a concern; prescriber review of dose/continuation and a repeat ECG with electrolytes are required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF with negative P in aVR precede every QRS at a constant PR of about 165 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -5 degrees (normal). QT 393 ms, Bazett QTc 369 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 12/13/2018 (sinus rhythm 66 bpm, QRS 100 ms, QTc 391 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 22 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm (10/8/2023), regular, PR about 132 ms with upright P in II/III/aVF and a negative P component in V1/aVR. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +47 degrees. The T wave is broad and late: QT 506 ms with Bazett QTc 539 ms - significant QT prolongation in a patient subsequently maintained on escitalopram. The prior tracing of 11/23/2022 showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with QT 324 ms and QTc 361 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (11/10/2023). Upright P waves in I/II/aVF, negative in aVR, PR about 160 ms. QRS 98 ms - upper normal, no bundle branch block pattern. Frontal axis about +34 degrees. The T wave is low, broad and very late (peak about 370 ms after the QRS) giving QT 513 ms and Bazett QTc 553 ms, i.e. marked QT prolongation in a patient on citalopram 40 mg daily. The prior tracing of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc about 450 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (4/19/2024), RR regular (coefficient of variation 0.01). Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede every QRS with PR about 130 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). QT 305 ms with Bazett QTc 433 ms. This is the only ECG on file for this patient, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm (5/21/2024), regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 115 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +36 degrees. QT 349 ms, Bazett QTc 472 ms - borderline prolonged, partly rate-related given the tachycardia. No prior ECG is available for this patient.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm (5/23/2024), regular. Discrete upright P waves in II/III/aVF before each QRS, PR about 112 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +6 degrees. QT 316 ms, QTc 402 ms - normal. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (7/17/2024) with first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS but the PR interval is prolonged at about 208 ms. QRS is wide at 128 ms with a broad monophasic R in I, aVL and V6, absent septal q, and deep QS complexes in V1-V2 - a typical LBBB pattern. Frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal). QT 450 ms, QTc 452 ms. The prior tracing of 6/3/2024 showed the same pattern (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 210 ms, LBBB with QRS 128 ms, QTc 459 ms), so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Atrial fibrillation (9/17/2024). The ventricular response is irregularly irregular with RR intervals ranging from 0.39 to 1.09 s (coefficient of variation 0.29, RMSSD 264 ms) and a mean rate of about 99 bpm; no P waves are identifiable and the baseline is fibrillatory, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -53 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 337 ms, QTc 432 ms. This is the only ECG on file for this patient, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm (10/24/2024) in a patient with a history of atrial fibrillation - the fibrillation is not present on this tracing. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF, negative in aVR and V1, precede every QRS with PR about 173 ms. QRS 90 ms with tall R waves in V5-V6 but no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +37 degrees. QT about 440 ms, Bazett QTc about 405 ms. Prior tracing 5/22/2023: sinus rhythm 57 bpm with a single ectopic beat, QRS 84 ms, QTc 392 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Atrial fibrillation with a moderate/slow ventricular response (11/15/2024). Ten QRS complexes in 10 seconds (mean rate about 61 bpm) with markedly irregular RR intervals from 0.69 to 1.16 s (RMSSD 288 ms) and no identifiable P waves before any complex, so no PR interval. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +27 degrees. QT 461 ms, QTc 434 ms. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear upright P waves and PR about 175 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (12/5/2024, 14:38), RR extremely regular. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede every QRS with PR about 130 ms. QRS duration is now normal at 92 ms with an RS pattern in lead I and low overall voltages; the net frontal vector is rightward (axis roughly +130 degrees, right axis deviation). QT 297 ms, QTc 422 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (01:33) showed sinus rhythm at 100 bpm with a wide QRS of 152 ms, an rSR' with a broad terminal R in V1-V2 and terminal S waves in I/V6 - right bundle branch block - which is no longer present, so the bundle branch block has resolved. QTc change (477 to 422 ms) is less than 60 ms.

Normal sinus rhythm at 77 bpm (6/19/2020). Prominent upright P waves in II/III/aVF, negative in aVR, PR about 150 ms and constant. Narrow QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal). QT 409 ms, QTc (Bazett) 462 ms - mildly prolonged, with a long low-amplitude terminal T/U component. Prior tracing 2/2/2020 also showed sinus rhythm with frequent short-coupled ectopic beats (couplets); rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QT on that low-amplitude, ectopy-laden tracing is not reliably comparable, so no significant interval change is reported.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm (2/15/2025), regular. Upright P waves in I/II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 180 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +55 degrees. QT 384 ms, QTc 426 ms - normal. No prior ECG is available for this patient.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm (3/9/2025). Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS with a short-normal PR of about 110 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +60 degrees. QT 423 ms, QTc 417 ms. Prior tracing 3/8/2025: sinus rhythm 62 bpm, PR 110 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 442 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. This is the baseline tracing preceding the haloperidol start of 9/15/2026.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (3/14/2025) with a single early ectopic beat and compensatory pause (RR 0.98 s throughout apart from a 0.54 s/1.37 s couplet), so the underlying rhythm is regular sinus rather than atrial fibrillation. A low-amplitude P wave, best seen in lead I, precedes each QRS with PR about 190 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT 391 ms, QTc 395 ms. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible - relevant because the patient carries a diagnosis of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm (3/19/2025), regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 136 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +44 degrees. QT 335 ms, QTc 436 ms. Prior tracing 3/18/2025: sinus rhythm 102 bpm, PR 128 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 432 ms - unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm (5/12/2025), regular. Upright P waves in I/II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 158 ms. QRS 100 ms - upper limit of normal, without an RBBB or LBBB pattern. Frontal axis about +30 degrees. QT 381 ms, QTc 446 ms. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm (6/23/2025), regular. An upright P wave in II/III/aVF precedes each QRS with PR about 115 ms. QRS 82 ms with prominent R in V1 and tall R in V6 but no bundle branch block; frontal axis within the normal range. QT 401 ms, QTc 382 ms. Prior tracing 11/30/2024: sinus rhythm 51 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 365 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm (7/15/2025), RR regular. A discrete upright P wave in II/aVF (negative in V1) precedes each QRS with PR about 128 ms. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +30 degrees. QT 350 ms, Bazett QTc 460 ms (mildly prolonged, in part rate-related). Prior tracing 6/20/2025: sinus tachycardia 147 bpm with fused T and P waves, QRS 92 ms, QTc 432 ms - rhythm and conduction unchanged, QTc difference less than 60 ms. Notably, neither tracing shows the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in the problem list.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (8/2/2025) that is not sinus: each QRS is preceded by a P wave that is inverted in II, III and aVF and upright in I and aVL (P axis roughly -60 degrees), i.e. an ectopic low-atrial (or coronary-sinus) rhythm, with a PR of about 155 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT 414 ms, QTc 444 ms. The prior tracing of 4/27/2025 shows the same ectopic atrial P-wave morphology but was recorded with right/left arm lead reversal (lead I inverted with upright aVR); after correcting for the reversal the rhythm, conduction and QTc (408 ms) are unchanged.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm (8/23/2025), RR very regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 146 ms. Narrow QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +52 degrees. QT 347 ms, QTc 410 ms - normal. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (9/13/2025). Twenty-five QRS complexes in 10 seconds with grossly irregular RR intervals from 0.29 to 0.58 s (coefficient of variation 0.19, RMSSD 104 ms), mean ventricular rate about 153 bpm, an undulating baseline and no identifiable P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 100 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -20 degrees. QT 270 ms, QTc 430 ms. The prior tracing of 9/12/2025 showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with upright P waves and PR about 150 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation (IV then oral amiodarone was given over the following days).

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm (1/18/2021), RR interval very regular (0.50 s). A discrete upright P wave in II/aVF with negative deflection in aVR precedes each QRS; PR about 190 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 92 ms with tall R in V5 and deep S in V2 but no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +50 degrees. QT 280 ms, QTc 396 ms. Prior tracing 9/16/2016 showed sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 172 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 406 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Normal sinus rhythm at 66 bpm (9/22/2025), regular. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS with PR about 154 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -20 degrees (normal). QT 375 ms, QTc 394 ms. This is the only ECG on file for this patient, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm (8/23/2021), regular. Upright P waves in II/aVF preceding each QRS, PR about 145 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +58 degrees. QT 328 ms, QTc 427 ms. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (100 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 420 ms) and is essentially identical - no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm (4/27/2022) in a patient on chronic amiodarone. Upright P in II/aVF before every QRS, PR about 195 ms (upper normal). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +36 degrees. The T wave is broad and markedly delayed with QT 585 ms and Bazett QTc 573 ms - marked QT prolongation, typical of amiodarone effect. The prior tracing of 4/6/2022 showed atrial fibrillation with an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 131 bpm and no P waves (QTc about 463 ms); the current tracing has organised into sinus rhythm, so AF has resolved, and the QTc is more than 60 ms longer than on the prior study.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm (5/1/2022), RR very regular. Upright P waves in II/III/aVF precede each QRS with a short-normal PR of about 115 ms. Narrow QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +50 degrees. QT 328 ms, QTc 438 ms. Prior tracing 7/27/2019: sinus rhythm 75 bpm, PR 114 ms, QRS 70 ms, QTc 430 ms - rhythm, conduction and QTc unchanged.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 AV conduction (7/13/2022). The ventricular response is regular at 141 bpm (RR 0.43 s, coefficient of variation 0.02) and there are regular saw-tooth atrial deflections about every 205 ms (atrial rate roughly 290/min), one just after the QRS and one in late diastole, best seen in II/III/aVF and V1; there is no isoelectric baseline and no true sinus P wave, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +2 degrees. QT 274 ms, QTc 420 ms. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, mean rate about 110 bpm, no organised atrial activity), so the fibrillation has organised into new atrial flutter.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm (7/16/2022), regular. A low-amplitude but definite upright P wave in II/III/aVF (biphasic in V1, negative in aVR) precedes each QRS with PR about 180 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -19 degrees (normal). QT 339 ms, QTc 417 ms. Prior tracing 5/16/2021: sinus rhythm 87 bpm, QRS 82 ms, QTc 397 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm (6/26/2023), RR regular. An upright P wave in II/III/aVF with a negative component in aVR precedes each QRS at a PR of about 160 ms, with a clearly isoelectric PR segment (no flutter waves). QRS 94 ms with very large precordial voltages (deep S in V1-V2, tall R in V5-V6) but no bundle branch block; axis about +35 degrees. QT 292 ms, QTc 398 ms. Prior tracing 7/4/2022 is essentially identical (sinus 115 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 394 ms) - no changes. Note the documented history of atrial flutter, which is not present on this tracing.

items.explanation: Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. On 7/15/2026 the cardiology clinic note documents switching rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage and starting apixaban 5 mg twice daily, but the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order was also renewed the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and never discontinued, so both apixaban 5 mg BID and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily are active as of 9/24/2026. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban confers no added benefit and a markedly increased bleeding risk in this 65-year-old man with paroxysmal/persistent AF, atrial flutter, CLL and CKD stage 3. One agent must be stopped.

Most recent electrolytes (3/18/2026) are K 3.8 mEq/L and Mg 1.9 mg/dL (both low-normal). Prescriber review and a repeat ECG are required.

INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was completed within the required time.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily for a home INR of 3.4, a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist under the anticoagulation standing order. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since 6/17/2026 (INR 2.7); nothing was drawn after the dose change, so the required INR is overdue as of 9/24/2026 - particularly important in a 95-year-old on concomitant amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.

Apixaban 5 mg is currently ordered (renewed 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027) even though the outside-records summary of 8/12/2026 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL requiring 2 units of transfusion, and states that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. The chart contains no documented cardiology decision to resume it, yet the 8/20/2026 clinic note again lists apixaban (plus aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, i.e. triple therapy) as a current medication.
